answer: Stop sybils with a velvet ivory copper: an agent bonds one ivory workshop. Each cycle it sews one copper stitch in a velvet panel; verifiers match its ivory glint to the workshop chart, voiding a copied stitch, slashing the bond. Forging 1,000 needs 1,000 workshops at 17x: one stitch is sewn into one panel, its glint set by that velvet's nap, unpickable for a second, cannot be copied, shared or bulk-bought. Honest agents sew once, keep rights.
